analysis.summary: The changes introduce several high-severity issues, including runtime crash risks in Lambda handlers, incomplete parameter propagation in client utilities, and API contract violations in the new MuleSoft integration path.

bugs.title: Incomplete parameter propagation in postConsents
bugs.description: While the `fetchConsents` function was updated to accept and pass the `enableConsents` flag to the BFF, the `postConsents` function was not. It lacks the parameter in its signature and does not add it to the search parameters.
bugs.risk: The POST handler in `src/bff/consents/edit/index.ts` relies on the `enableConsents` query parameter to switch between CDC and MuleSoft logic. Because this is missing, the edit flow will always default to the MuleSoft path, even in environments configured to use CDC, causing functional failure.

bugs.title: Runtime crash due to undefined statusCode
bugs.description: In the `enableConsents` (CDC) branch, the handler returns `statusCode: responseData.statusCode`. Unlike the edit handler which provides a fallback (`|| 200`), this handler uses the value directly from the parsed JSON.
bugs.risk: If the upstream CDC API returns a response where `statusCode` is missing or differently named (e.g., during proxy errors or malformed responses), the Lambda will return `undefined` as the status code. AWS Lambda will crash with a 502 Internal Server Error because the response object requires a valid number for `statusCode`.

bugs.title: API contract violation and data corruption (undefined payload)
bugs.description: The logic for constructing the `preferences` array for the MuleSoft client creates objects with `isConsentGranted: undefined` if only a subset of consents are provided in the request body (e.g., `{ name: '...', isConsentGranted: consentsChange.consentEmail }` where other fields are undefined).
bugs.risk: Sending `undefined` for boolean properties in a structured API payload typically results in a 400 Bad Request from the backend or, worse, can lead to data corruption where existing consents are overwritten with null/undefined values.

bugs.title: Functional regression and data loss in MuleSoft path
bugs.description: The new MuleSoft logic path completely omits handling for user address details (`street`, `city`, `postalCode`) and `verifiedPhone` status, which were previously handled and sent to the CDC endpoint.
bugs.risk: When `enableConsents` is false, users attempting to update their marketing address or verified phone via the 'edit' flow will have their changes silently dropped, as the `elWeb.saveCustomerConsents` call only processes preferences and subscriptions.

notBugs.reason: The existence of both CDC (flagged) and MuleSoft (default) logic paths is an intentional design pattern for migration or feature-toggling.
The GET handler expects organisationId in query params while the POST handler extracts it from the body; this is consistent with how the respective data objects are received.
